promotion.assessment: The probe supplied the first candidates (Suunto Ocean, Suunto Nautic S, Garmin Descent G2) and moved no criterion. Discovery by class query alone is incomplete: models the agent knows to document scuba modes (Garmin Descent Mk3, fenix 8, Huawei Watch Ultimate) did not appear on the first page, so a named-model probe follows and is recorded as agent-supplied, not shelf-discovered.

actions.purpose: Reconnaissance of how dive-capable smartwatches are listed on Amazon.de: two class queries without brand names, first search page each, up to ten product pages per query, search pages retained.
actions.question: Do class queries surface smartwatches with a scuba dive mode at all, and which of the plan's properties (GPS, heart rate, barometer, dive mode, depth rating, NFC payment, Android compatibility, display, battery) do listings state?

result.next_action: probe-2: named-model queries for dive-capable smartwatches the class queries did not surface (Garmin Descent Mk3, Descent G1, fenix 8, tactix 8, Huawei Watch Ultimate), recorded as agent-supplied candidates.
result.summary: 22 responses, 20 product pages, 2 search pages, no challenges. Query 1 (Smartwatch Tauchcomputer) surfaced three dive-capable smartwatches: Suunto Ocean (3 colour ASINs, 799 EUR), Suunto Nautic S (549 EUR), Garmin Descent G2 (2 colour ASINs, 588-650 EUR), beside cheap generic smartwatches and the Suunto D5 dive computer. Query 2 (Tauchcomputer Uhr GPS NFC) returned pure dive computers (Cressi, Mares) and noise; NFC in a query does not select for payment. Listings state dive mode, depth, display and GPS runtime; none of the three dive-capable smartwatches states NFC payment in its bullets, so payment and EN 13319 are read from manufacturer specifications.

promotion.assessment: Candidates were supplied by the agent from manufacturer documentation, not discovered on the shelf; the comparison must say so, and the class-query probe stands as the shelf-discovered baseline.

actions.question: Are Garmin Descent Mk3/Mk3i, Descent G1, fenix 8, tactix 8 and Huawei Watch Ultimate listed on Amazon.de, at what price, and do their listings state a scuba mode, depth rating, NFC payment, Android compatibility, display and GPS runtime?

actions.purpose: Fetch by ASIN the seven product pages that probe-2's search pages sighted but did not open and that may be candidates: Garmin Descent Mk3 43 mm stainless and bronze, Descent Mk3i 51 mm, Descent G1, fenix 9 51 mm, fenix 8 Pro 51 mm, Huawei Watch Ultimate 2 green.

result.summary: 7 responses, 7 product pages by ASIN, no challenges. Contents read in the next step.

actions.purpose: Hand-read comparison of the candidates from probes 1-3 against the plan's requirements, using manufacturer manuals and specification pages recorded as plan sources; no executable brief exists because 'smartwatch' is not a registered category.
actions.question: Which listed Android-compatible smartwatches document a scuba decompression computer, NFC payment usable in Germany and GPS/HR/barometer, and how do they order on manufacturer-stated GPS runtime and display?

actions.purpose: Proposal, not funded: a 'smartwatch' category as a task experiment -- classifier over titles and breadcrumbs (Smartwatches node; excludes bands, pure dive computers and accessories), claim keys gps, heart_rate_sensor, barometric_altimeter, scuba_dive_mode, nfc_payment, android_compatible; axes price, gps_runtime_hours (unit-ambiguous across vendors: GPS-only vs all-systems vs expedition), depth_rating_m, display_type. Needs committed cases from the three probe feeds and counterexamples (Suunto Nautic S: dive computer without optical HR; fenix E: no dive). Execution is R15's.

Re-read the retained probe feeds and plan sources under plan revision 6 after the independent intake review of revision 5 failed: quality and style carried as unassessed hard conditions, the agent's proxies labelled as its own, the report rewritten to claim no more than the plan supports. No new marketplace request.
actions.question: Does the retained evidence still support the candidate table once nothing is admitted as 'passed' on measurement quality or style, and which rows compare on runtime?

actions.purpose: R15 phase 2: run the study over the three retained probe feeds under the smartwatch category adopted through engineer-1, bound to plan revision 7, its limited intake review and this ledger; compare the category's candidate table with the hand-read table of analyse-2 and explain every difference. No new marketplace request; the feeds are the committed evidence of 2026-09-18.
actions.question: Does the category, replayed over the same 57 records, admit the candidates the hand-read comparison admitted and state the same vendor claims -- and where it differs, is the difference the classifier's declared limit, a claim pattern, or an error?

actions.purpose: Second adaptation through R15: repair the smartwatch category's scuba_dive_mode claim, whose pattern the study revision (analyse-3) found admitting a water-resistance sentence ('tauchfähig bis 40m') and freediving ('Freitauchen bis zu 45 Metern', 'Apnoe') as a stated dive function -- the substitution plan revision 7's dive_computer forbids. Method version 2 of the category; the KOSPET Tank T4 listing becomes the counterexample. No marketplace request.
actions.question: Once the claim reads only a stated scuba function (a dive mode, dive computer, nitrox or a decompression model), which of the 20 listings that carried it keep it, and does any committed decision move beyond the claim itself?

actions.purpose: Re-derive the study of analyse-3 under the category's method version 2 (engineer-2): the same brief, plan revision 7 and feeds, bound to the second adaptation record, so that the study id carries the new method and the dive claim's change is read from the cards. No new marketplace request.
actions.question: Under the repaired dive claim, which rows lose scuba_dive_mode, and does any candidate, price or outcome decision move?

actions.purpose: R15 phase 4, the extraction case's bounded inspection (plan revision 7, ordering and dive_computer): read the three retained run stores and the 57 committed records for the layer the battery-runtime and dive statements live in. Found: 16 of 55 product pages carry an A+ comparison table (premium-module-5) whose cells for OTHER products are flattened into content.aplus.text and read by the vendor-text search as this product's statement; on B0DSC8GLRX the table does not contain the product at all and its card shows a 40 h GPS runtime that belongs to the Instinct 3 45 mm; the own column is identifiable by the ASIN its header links in 10 of 16 tables and carries mode-labelled runtimes ('Akkulaufzeit GPS-Modus: Bis zu 47 Stunden'). Layer: extraction (blocks.aplus_content) and evidence (validation.evidence.text_fields). No marketplace request.
actions.question: Is the runtime-with-mode gap a property of the page any category needs, lost or misassigned by the current path, or an interpretation the category can make over text it already receives?

actions.purpose: Third adaptation through R15, extraction layer: publish the A+ comparison table as structure -- content.aplus.prose (A+ text without table cells) and content.aplus.comparison (columns with the ASIN each header links, rows, and the index of this product's own column when its ASIN is linked) -- and let the vendor-text search read prose instead of the flattened text and the own column's rows as labelled statements. Schema v6 keys added, none changed; old records without the new keys read as before. Reproduction: B0DSC8GLRX loses the 40 h GPS runtime that belongs to another model; the fenix 8 sizes keep theirs from their own column with the mode in the label. No marketplace request.
actions.question: Once comparison-table cells about other products stop counting as this product's text, which runtime and claim values move on the 55 records, and does any committed decision move beyond them?

actions.purpose: Re-derive the study over the three probe feeds re-extracted offline from their retained pages under the third adaptation (engineer-4): the same brief and plan revision 7, bound to the aplus-comparison record, so the cards read A+ prose and the own comparison column instead of the flattened table. No new marketplace request.
actions.question: Which runtime and claim values move once another product's comparison cells stop counting as this product's text, and does any candidate, price or outcome decision move?

actions.purpose: Fourth adaptation through R15, category layer: repair the smartwatch category's nfc_payment claim, whose pattern credits a bare 'NFC' in a connectivity row as a payment statement -- six of the twenty positives on the retained records (both Huawei Watch Ultimate 2 listings, two GT 7 Pro, the Watch D3, the Amazfit Active Max) rest on that word alone, against the claim's own 'why' (NFC and a payment service on the page). Found by the independent intake review of plan revision 8 (adequacy A8.1). Method version 3; the pattern requires a payment service or contactless-payment phrase; NFC alone stays not_claimed with the reason. No marketplace request.
actions.question: Once the payment claim needs a payment-service statement, which of the twenty listings that carried it keep it, and does any committed decision move beyond the claim itself?

actions.purpose: Re-derive the study of analyse-5 under the category's method version 3 (engineer-5): the same brief over the re-extracted feeds and plan revision 7, bound to the nfc-payment-claim record, so the study id carries the new method and the payment claim's change is read from the cards. No new marketplace request.
actions.question: Under the repaired payment claim, which rows lose nfc_payment, and does any candidate, price or outcome decision move?
